newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cemig sale reset for May 28.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cemig sale reset for May 28.

text.p: Brazil's BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar) said it has rescheduled the auction of a 32.9 percent stake in Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig to May 28.

The sale of 18.7 million debentures convertible to a 32.9 percent voting stake in Cemig will take place at 0900 local/1200 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, BNDESPar said in a published statement Wednesday.
It noted, however, pre-qualified investors would be notified if a court injunction against the sale was maintained, preventing the auction from being held as planned.

Last month, a judge granted an injunction to halt the auction, previously scheduled for May 6. But Minas Gerais state officials had said it was unlikely that the auction would be delayed because the injunction would be appealed.
The Cemig sale ended up being delayed because companies pre-qualified for the auction asked for more time to visit the firm.

Five firms -- Southern Electric Brasil Participacoes Ltda, Copel, Pacific Generation Development Company, CEA Americas Inc. and Grupo CEA, comprising Artica Investment Group and CEA group -- have prequalified for the auction.
Cemig is owned by Minas Gerais state but the stake being sold was transferred to BNDESPar late last year to cover a 430 million reais state debt.
BNDESPar is the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES).
